items.name: Street of the new address
items.description: The street of the address the employee is moving to.
items.form: Part of the new address: street, number, postcode, town and country.

needed_by.purpose: Update the employee's master data and send documents (e.g. payslips) to the correct address.

items.name: House number of the new address
items.description: The house number of the address the employee is moving to.
items.form: Part of the new address: street, number, postcode, town and country.

needed_by.purpose: Update the employee's master data and send documents to the correct address.

items.notes: The meeting did not discuss addresses without a house number; whether it may be left empty is not stated.

items.name: Postcode of the new address
items.description: The postcode of the address the employee is moving to.
items.form: Part of the new address: street, number, postcode, town and country.

needed_by.purpose: Update the employee's master data and send documents to the correct address.

items.name: Town of the new address
items.description: The town of the address the employee is moving to.
items.form: Part of the new address: street, number, postcode, town and country.

needed_by.purpose: Update the employee's master data and send documents to the correct address.

items.name: Country of the new address
items.description: The country the employee is moving to (the new country of residence). It shows whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad.
items.form: Part of the new address: street, number, postcode, town and country. Country written as its English name, e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany".

needed_by.purpose: Update the employee's master data and send documents to the correct address; tell whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad.
Find out about moves abroad, because the employee may then be subject to source tax.

items.name: Valid from
items.description: The date from which the new address applies.
items.required_when: Always. It may be in the past, but not more than three months ago (see rule valid_from_within_three_months).

needed_by.purpose: Know which address to use for documents, in particular the payslips sent out on the 25th.

items.name: New canton
items.description: The Swiss canton the employee is moving to. Only needed if the employee moves to a different canton.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee moves within Switzerland to a different canton than before. Not asked if the move stays in the same canton or is abroad.

needed_by.purpose: Pass the change of canton to the tax office.

items.notes: The meeting did not say how a canton change is found out before the new canton is known (see OQ-01). The internal condition can only check this once both cantons are known.

items.name: Previous canton
items.description: The Swiss canton the employee lived in before the move. It is used only to tell whether the canton changes.
items.asked_when: Only for moves within Switzerland. It is open whether the employee is asked or HR takes it from its own employee records (see OQ-01).
items.required_when: For moves within Switzerland, so HR can tell whether the canton changes

needed_by.purpose: Tell whether the employee moves to a different canton, so the new canton is asked only when needed.

items.notes: Data minimisation (G-01) suggests not asking the employee if HR already has this information.

rules.name: Payroll must be informed of a move abroad
rules.statement: If the employee moves abroad (the new country is not Switzerland), payroll must be informed, because the employee may then be subject to source tax. For moves within Switzerland, payroll does not have to be informed.

table.then: Payroll does not have to be informed
Payroll must be informed (the employee may be subject to source tax)

rules.name: Move to a different canton
rules.statement: A move within Switzerland changes canton when the new canton is different from the previous canton. Only then is the new canton needed for the tax office.
inputs: New canton compared with previous canton

table.then: Canton changes – new canton is needed for the tax office
Canton does not change – new canton is not asked
Not applicable (move abroad) – new canton is not asked

rules.expression: new_country == "Switzerland" and is_set(previous_canton) and is_set(new_canton) and new_canton != previous_canton

rules.name: Valid-from date at most three months in the past
rules.statement: The valid-from date may be in the past, because people often report late, but not more than three months before the day the employee reports the move. The meeting set no limit for future dates.
inputs: Valid from compared with three months before today

when: On or after the date three months before today
Before the date three months before today

open_questions.question: How do we find out whether the canton changes for a move within Switzerland? Options: ask the employee for the new canton on every Swiss move, ask them whether the canton changes, or have HR compare the new address with the canton it already has on record.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The new canton should be asked only when the canton changes, but that can't be known without the new canton or the previous canton. Data minimisation (G-01) argues against asking for anything HR already holds.
options: Ask 'Are you moving to a different canton?' and ask for the new canton only if the answer is yes
HR takes the previous canton from its own records, and the new canton is worked out from the new address or asked only when it differs
Always ask for the new canton on Swiss moves and keep it only if it changed
open_questions.recommendation: Clarify with HR (Sara). Prefer taking the previous canton from HR's existing records so the employee is not asked for data HR already has.

open_questions.question: Is there a latest allowed valid-from date in the future?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The meeting gave only a limit for past dates. Without a limit for the future, a move could be reported for any date ahead.
options: A fixed future limit (e.g. a number of months ahead)
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR. Until then, apply no future limit.

open_questions.question: Does 'not more than three months ago' include a date exactly three months back, and what happens if the employee reports an older date (rejected, or passed to HR for manual handling)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It sets the exact cut-off date and what happens to a late report that misses it.
options: Exactly three months back is allowed; older dates are rejected
Exactly three months back is allowed; older dates go to HR for manual handling
open_questions.recommendation: Treat a date exactly three months back as allowed, and confirm with HR how older reports are handled.

open_questions.question: Does 'move abroad' always mean the new country is not Switzerland? What about employees who already live abroad and move within their country or into Switzerland?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The payroll rule assumes employees currently live in Switzerland. Cross-border staff could be informed wrongly, or not at all.
options: Any new country other than Switzerland means payroll is informed
Payroll is informed whenever the country of residence changes (including moves into Switzerland)

open_questions.question: Does payroll need any further information from the employee for a move abroad (to assess source tax), beyond the new country and the valid-from date?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only HR was interviewed. HR said the employee 'may' be subject to source tax, and Sara thinks the list is complete only 'for now'. Payroll's own needs are unknown.
open_questions.recommendation: Talk to payroll before finalising the questions for moves abroad.

open_questions.question: Is there a fixed list of countries the employee can choose from?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No source defines the allowed countries. Only the wording (English names) is given.
open_questions.recommendation: Use all countries, written by their English names (G-02), unless HR or payroll restricts them.

exclusions.reason: HR explicitly does not want to know why people move. It is private and must not be asked.

features.title: Capture the new address
features.goal: HR gets the complete new address of a moving employee so master data is updated and documents such as payslips reach the right address.
features.context: When an employee moves, HR has to update the employee master data and send documents to the new address (F-TR-001, F-TR-006, F-TR-013). The new address is street, house number, postcode, town and country, all needed every time (F-TR-016). The country also shows whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad, which the payroll and canton features depend on (F-TR-010). Countries are written by their English names (G-02). Only what HR needs is asked (G-01). The reason for the move is explicitly excluded (EX-01, F-TR-009). This feature comes first because every other feature builds on the new address, and especially on the country.

stories.title: Report the street, house number, postcode and town of the new address
stories.i_want: every employee who reports a move to give me the street, house number, postcode and town of their new address
stories.so_that: I can update the employee master data and send documents such as payslips to the correct address
stories.priority_reason: Without the new address HR cannot update master data and documents such as payslips go to the wrong address. Every other part of the address change depends on it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Street, house number, postcode and town are always asked and must be given
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address
acceptance_criteria.when: they give their new address
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for the street, house number, postcode and town of the new address, whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad, and the report cannot be completed while any of these four is missing

acceptance_criteria.title: HR receives the new address
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has completed their change of address report
acceptance_criteria.when: HR looks at the report
acceptance_criteria.then: HR has the street, house number, postcode and town of the new address and can update the master data and send documents such as payslips there

acceptance_criteria.title: The reason for the move is never asked
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address
acceptance_criteria.when: they go through the questions
acceptance_criteria.then: they are not asked why they are moving, because that is private and HR does not want to know it

stories.title: Report the country of the new address
stories.i_want: every employee who reports a move to give me the country of their new address, written by its English name
stories.so_that: I have the complete address for master data and documents, and I can tell whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad
stories.priority_reason: The country completes the address and decides whether the move is abroad; the payroll (source tax) and canton steps depend on it.

acceptance_criteria.title: The country is always asked and must be given
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address
acceptance_criteria.when: they give their new address
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for the country of the new address, and the report cannot be completed without it, whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad

acceptance_criteria.title: Countries are written by their English names
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee gives the country of the new address
acceptance_criteria.when: the country is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it is shown by its English name, for example "Switzerland" or "Germany". Whether employees choose from a fixed list of countries or from all countries is still open (see OQ-06); until it is decided, no country is excluded

acceptance_criteria.title: HR receives the country and can tell a move abroad from a move within Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has completed their change of address report
acceptance_criteria.when: HR looks at the report
acceptance_criteria.then: HR has the country of the new address, can use it for master data and documents, and can see whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad (the new country of residence)

features.title: Date from which the new address applies
features.goal: HR knows from which date to use the new address, in particular for the payslips sent out on the 25th, and still accepts moves reported late within a fixed window.
features.context: HR needs to know which address applies when documents go out, especially the payslips sent on the 25th (F-TR-007, F-TR-008, F-TR-018). People often report their move late, so a valid-from date in the past must be accepted, but not more than three months back (F-TR-019, F-TR-020). The meeting set no limit for future dates (F-TR-021). Dates use the format DD.MM.YYYY (G-02). Still open: the exact cut-off, how older dates are handled, and whether there is a future limit.

stories.title: Report the date from which the new address applies
stories.i_want: every address change to include the date from which the new address applies
stories.so_that: I know which address to use for documents, in particular the payslips sent out on the 25th
stories.priority_reason: HR states the date is always required and that without it they cannot do anything, so the process is blocked without it (F-TR-018); it decides the address on payslips (F-TR-008).

acceptance_criteria.title: Valid-from date is always asked and cannot be left empty
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address, whether within Switzerland or abroad
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the details of the move
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is always asked from which date the new address applies, and the report cannot be completed without this date

acceptance_criteria.title: Valid-from date is given as a calendar date in the agreed wording
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee states from which date the new address applies
acceptance_criteria.when: the date is recorded and shown
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a single calendar date written as DD.MM.YYYY (for example 01.12.2026)

acceptance_criteria.title: HR receives the valid-from date with the new address
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has completed an address change report
acceptance_criteria.when: HR receives the report
acceptance_criteria.then: HR sees the valid-from date together with the new address, so it can decide which address applies to documents going out, such as the payslips on the 25th

stories.title: Accept late reports up to three months back
stories.i_want: to report my move even if the move has already happened, as long as it was not more than three months ago
stories.so_that: a late report is still accepted and HR can correct my address, while HR is not asked to handle moves that lie too far back
stories.priority_reason: Late reporting is common (F-TR-020); without accepting past dates many real reports could not be made, and HR set an explicit three-month limit (F-TR-019).

acceptance_criteria.title: Past date within three months is accepted
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a move whose valid-from date is in the past, on or after the date three months before the day of reporting
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the valid-from date
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is accepted and the report can be completed

examples.name: Exactly three months back (cut-off to be confirmed, see OQ-03)

acceptance_criteria.title: Date more than three months back is not accepted
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a move whose valid-from date is before the date three months before the day of reporting
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the valid-from date
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is not accepted and the employee is told that a valid-from date may lie at most three months in the past; what happens to such a report afterwards (rejected or passed to HR for manual handling) is still open, see OQ-03

examples.name: One day beyond the three-month window

acceptance_criteria.title: Today and future dates are accepted
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a move that applies from today or from a date in the future
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the valid-from date
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is accepted; no latest future date applies until HR confirms whether one is needed (see OQ-02)

features.title: Inform payroll about moves abroad
features.goal: Payroll is reliably informed whenever an employee moves abroad, so it can check whether source tax applies, and is not involved in moves within Switzerland.
features.context: An employee who moves abroad may become subject to source tax, so payroll has to be told (F-TR-010, F-TR-011, F-TR-012). For moves within Switzerland payroll does not need to know (F-TR-013, F-TR-016), so it should not be informed (G-01). The decision uses the new country captured in FEAT-01 and the valid-from date from FEAT-02. Only HR was interviewed. Payroll's own information needs and how cross-border employees are handled are still open (F-TR-022).

stories.title: Payroll is informed when an employee moves abroad
stories.i_want: to be informed whenever an employee reports a move to a country other than Switzerland
stories.so_that: I can check whether the employee is now subject to source tax and handle it correctly
stories.priority_reason: HR states payroll 'has to be informed' of moves abroad; a missed notification puts the source-tax obligation at risk (F-TR-011, F-TR-012).

acceptance_criteria.title: Move abroad informs payroll
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address and the country of the new address is any country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the address change
acceptance_criteria.then: payroll is informed of the move abroad, including the new country of residence, so it can check whether source tax applies. Whether payroll needs any further information from the employee for this check is still open (see OQ-05).

acceptance_criteria.title: Country is always known for the payroll decision
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in the new address
acceptance_criteria.then: the country of the new address is always asked and must be given, written as its English name (e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany"), so it is always clear whether payroll has to be informed. The country is received by HR and, for moves abroad, by payroll.

stories.title: Payroll is not involved in moves within Switzerland
stories.i_want: my move within Switzerland not to be passed on to payroll
stories.so_that: my personal data is shared only with those who need it for my case
stories.priority_reason: Data-minimisation principle (G-01); HR said only the address is needed for Swiss moves (F-TR-013, F-TR-016). No incident or blocked process is reported.

acceptance_criteria.title: Move within Switzerland does not inform payroll
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a change of address and the country of the new address is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the address change
acceptance_criteria.then: payroll is not informed of the move; HR handles the address change (and, if the canton changes, the tax office notification) on its own. How employees who currently live abroad and move into Switzerland or within their foreign country are treated is still open (see OQ-04).

features.title: Capture a change of canton for the tax office
features.goal: When an employee moves to a different Swiss canton, HR gets the new canton and can pass the change to the tax office, without asking for the canton in any other case.
features.context: For a move within Switzerland to a different canton, HR has to pass the new canton to the tax office (F-TR-014, F-TR-016). If the move stays in the same canton or goes abroad, the canton is not needed and must not be asked (F-TR-015, G-01). To see whether the canton changes, the previous canton is compared with the new one (F-TR-017). The previous canton might already be in HR's records. How the change is detected is not yet decided, and this blocks the feature (OQ-01). It comes last because it depends on the country from FEAT-01 and on that decision.

stories.title: HR receives the new canton when the employee moves to a different canton
stories.i_want: to receive the new canton whenever an employee moves within Switzerland to a different canton
stories.so_that: I can pass the change of canton to the tax office
stories.priority_reason: HR states the new canton is needed for the tax office (F-TR-014); without it HR cannot meet its reporting duty for a change of canton. Delivery is blocked until OQ-01 is decided.

acceptance_criteria.title: New canton is asked and required when the canton changes
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a move whose new country is Switzerland and whose new canton differs from the previous canton
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reports the change of address
acceptance_criteria.then: the new canton is asked and must be given; the move counts as a change of canton. How the change is recognised before the new canton is known is still open (see OQ-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: HR receives the new canton for the tax office
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has reported a move to a different Swiss canton and given the new canton
acceptance_criteria.when: the report is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: HR receives the new canton together with the new address, so it can pass the change of canton to the tax office. No other stakeholder receives the new canton.

acceptance_criteria.title: Form of the new canton
acceptance_criteria.given: the new canton is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the new canton
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee names a Swiss canton. The sources define no further list or wording for cantons.

stories.title: Employee is not asked for a canton when it is not needed
stories.i_want: not to be asked for a new canton when I move within the same canton or abroad
stories.so_that: I only give information that HR actually needs for me
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a product guideline (G-01) and HR explicitly said the canton is not needed within the same canton (F-TR-015); asking anyway causes no blocked process but adds needless questions.

acceptance_criteria.title: No new canton for a move within the same canton
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee moves within Switzerland and stays in the same canton
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reports the change of address
acceptance_criteria.then: only the new address is asked; the new canton is not asked and the move does not count as a change of canton. How this is recognised without asking for the canton is still open (see OQ-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: No new canton for a move abroad
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee moves to a country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reports the change of address
acceptance_criteria.then: the new canton is not asked and the change-of-canton rule does not apply.

stories.title: HR knows the previous canton for moves within Switzerland
stories.i_want: the employee's previous canton to be known for every move within Switzerland
stories.so_that: I can tell whether the canton changes and the new canton is asked only when needed
stories.priority_reason: The change of canton cannot be determined without the previous canton (F-TR-017), so US-04.1 and US-04.2 depend on it; how it is obtained is the blocking open question OQ-01.

acceptance_criteria.title: Previous canton is needed for moves within Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reports a move whose new country is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the change of address is reported
acceptance_criteria.then: the previous canton is known and must be available so HR can compare it with the new canton. Whether the employee is asked for it or HR takes it from its own employee records is still open (see OQ-01); following data minimisation, the employee should not be asked for what HR already holds.

acceptance_criteria.title: Previous canton is not needed for moves abroad
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee moves to a country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the change of address is reported
acceptance_criteria.then: the previous canton is not asked, because no change of canton has to be determined.

acceptance_criteria.title: Previous canton is used only to detect the change
acceptance_criteria.given: the previous canton is known for a move within Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: HR processes the report
acceptance_criteria.then: the previous canton is used by HR only to tell whether the canton changes; it is not passed to any other stakeholder.
